danny.audio_profile: Danny, a regular guy in his late thirties. He is genuinely a little scared and still shaken, and he tells what happened plainly and honestly, in a natural voice with little inflection, like a real person, not an actor.

marcus.audio_profile: Marcus, 22, a big, easygoing young man with a deep voice, talking low into his walkie-talkie.

scene: A man quietly tells what happened during the first hour of a zombie outbreak at the mall where he works. Close to the microphone, plain and natural, no music.
sample_context: A first-person story told plainly, in a natural, slightly scared voice.

chunks.text: Right now there's a zombie pressed up against my gate, and it's wearing my best friend's uniform.
The radio on his chest is about to tell every one of them exactly where I'm hiding.

lines.text: An hour ago, I was basically the king of this mall.

chunks.text: I'm Danny. I do night security at Maplecrest Mall, and yeah, I've heard every mall cop joke there is.
I work nights for one reason. At three-fifteen every afternoon, I'm standing at the bus stop when my daughter Lily gets off.
She's seven, and she thinks I'm the king of the mall, because I carry forty-two keys, one for every store.
Tonight, I'd only need one of them.
The job's pretty simple. I walk the loop, I rattle the gates, and around one a.m., Marcus calls me from down in the parking garage.
Marcus is twenty-two, he's studying to be a nurse, and he tells the worst jokes you've ever heard.
Tonight he calls at one-forty, and there's no joke. He's whispering.
[low, tense] Danny. There's a guy on the ramp. He's walking... wrong.
